files.why: Add a zod server-shape DTO for the per-client reschedule-toggle response so the runtime flag is validated at the data boundary.
Add fetchRescheduleEnabled(clientId) that reads the toggle from the API via httpTransport at runtime — this is what makes it flippable without a deploy.
Add an MSW handler + per-client seed for the new flag endpoint so dev and tests can exercise on/off states.
New composable that loads the flag reactively and exposes a boolean the view can gate on, keeping clock/IO wiring out of the .vue file (mirrors useDaySchedule/useReschedule).
Hide the Reschedule button and RescheduleForm when the flag is off — the actual on/off behavior the user sees.
Cover fetchRescheduleEnabled returning enabled/disabled per client, following the tests/ naming convention (scheduling.core.test.ts already exists).

uncertain: Whether the toggle belongs in UI+data only or should also become a core/policy rule (e.g. canReschedule taking a featureEnabled arg). I placed it as a UI gate + IO fetch because the value is IO-sourced and core is framework-free/pure; folding an externally-fetched flag into a pure domain rule felt like over-reach, but a team that treats 'is this flow available' as a domain invariant might want it in core/policy.ts.

Whether scheduling/index.ts needs a new export. Reschedule only appears in DayView today, so no cross-slice/app consumer needs the flag — but if the app shell or ClientOverviewView must also react to it, the query/composable would have to be exposed via the public surface.

Whether a data/mappers.ts change is needed. A bare boolean flag needs no real DTO->core mapping, so I left mappers out; if the server returns a richer shape (e.g. rollout metadata) a mapper entry would be required.
Test file naming/location: tests live in apps/web/tests/ named <slice>.<area>.test.ts; I assumed scheduling.data.test.ts is the right new name, but the team may prefer extending an existing file.
questions: What does 'per customer' mean here — the end-client (clientId like c-ana, already a domain noun) or the product tenant/organization using Vise? There is no current-customer/auth concept in the repo today, and DayView renders a mixed-client day, so per-client gating on that specific view is ambiguous. Which identity keys the flag, and where does it come from?

Is the flag served by our own API (so transport + a data query is enough) or a third-party flag service like LaunchDarkly (which would add a shared provider/bootstrap and likely an app/providers entry)?
What is the real backend contract for the toggle — endpoint path, payload shape, and default when the client is unknown? Only MSW mocks exist now.
Freshness/caching: 'without deploying' implies a runtime fetch, but how live must it be — evaluated once per page load, or must an in-session flip take effect without reload?

When the flow is OFF, should the Reschedule affordance disappear entirely, be disabled with a message, and should the server-side reschedule endpoint also reject (so the toggle isn't purely cosmetic/bypassable)?
